sentences.en: Raise the flag, the ranks tightly closed, the SA marches with calm, steady step.
sentences.zh: 升起旗帜，队伍紧密靠拢，冲锋队迈着沉着稳健的步伐前进。

sentences.en: Comrades shot by the Red Front and reactionaries march in spirit within our ranks.
sentences.zh: 被红色阵线和反动派杀害的同志们，在我们的队伍中精神永存。

sentences.en: Clear the streets for the brown battalions, clear the streets for the storm division man.
sentences.zh: 为褐色营队清空街道，为冲锋队员清空街道。

sentences.en: Millions are looking upon the hooked cross full of hope, the day of freedom and of bread dawns.
sentences.zh: 数百万人满怀希望地注视着万字旗，自由与面包的黎明即将到来。

sentences.en: For the last time the call to arms is sounded, for the fight we all stand prepared.
sentences.zh: 战斗的号角最后一次吹响，我们所有人已做好战斗准备。

sentences.en: Already Hitler's banners fly over all streets.
sentences.zh: 希特勒的旗帜已在所有街道上飘扬。

sentences.en: The time of bondage will last but a little while now.
sentences.zh: 束缚的时代现在只会再持续一小会儿了。

sentences.en: Those are the English translation of the Horst Vessel song, which Dominic, I think I'm correct in saying, ended up kind of the anthem of Germany, didn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是《霍斯特·威塞尔之歌》的英文翻译，多米尼克，我想我没说错吧，这首歌最终成了德国的国歌，对吗？

sentences.en: Along with Deutschland über alles, once the Nazis had taken power.
sentences.zh: 在纳粹掌权后，它与《德意志高于一切》并列。

sentences.en: And it was, of course, written by a man called Horst Vessel, so hence its name.
sentences.zh: 当然，它是由一个叫霍斯特·威塞尔的人写的，所以才有了这个名字。

sentences.en: And Horst Vessel is pretty much the only time I've ever written about the rise of the Nazis, because it featured in Dominion.
sentences.zh: 关于纳粹崛起，我几乎只写过霍斯特·威塞尔，因为他出现在了《统治》一书中。

sentences.en: And as I was writing about Horst Vessel, I was kind of obviously looking at, you know, echoes of parodies of Christianity.
sentences.zh: 当我写到霍斯特·威塞尔时，我显然是在观察，你知道，基督教模仿者的回响。

sentences.en: And I hadn't fully appreciated the background to the story, which is what this episode is basically about.
sentences.zh: 我之前并没有完全理解这个故事的背景，而这正是本集主要讲述的内容。

sentences.en: So it's the process by which the Great Depression hits Germany, street fights between the Nazis and the communists intensify.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是大萧条席卷德国，纳粹与共产党之间街头斗争加剧的过程。

sentences.en: And towards the end of it, we move towards Hitler actually taking power.
sentences.zh: 在这一过程接近尾声时，我们转向了希特勒真正掌权的阶段。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Last week, we did two episodes about the rise of the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 上周，我们做了两集关于纳粹崛起的节目。

sentences.en: So the origins, the intellectual and political origins of Nazism, and then the story of Hitler in the 1920s, or for much of the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 讲述了纳粹主义的思想和政治起源，以及希特勒在20世纪20年代大部分时间里的故事。

sentences.en: And this episode is the sort of the crunch point, I suppose, is the point at which the Nazis take power.
sentences.zh: 而这一集是所谓的关键点，我想，也就是纳粹夺取政权的时刻。

sentences.en: So we left them with the Nazis as a small party, but expanding, particularly in the Protestant countryside and the late 1920s against the backdrop of the Weimar Republic,
sentences.zh: 我们上次讲到纳粹还是一个小党派，但在20世纪20年代末魏玛共和国的背景下，特别是在新教乡村地区不断扩张，

sentences.en: united under a leader in Adolf Hitler, who has the gift of the gab and has become convinced that he is the man of destiny who will lead Germany to greatness.
sentences.zh: 在阿道夫·希特勒这位领导人的团结下，他口才出众，并深信自己是带领德国走向伟大的天选之人。

sentences.en: And Tom, you were very keen to talk about Horst Wessel.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你非常热衷于谈论霍斯特·威塞尔。

sentences.en: So Horst Wessel is a young man who joins the Nazi party in, I think, 1926.
sentences.zh: 霍斯特·威塞尔是一个年轻人，我想他在1926年加入了纳粹党。

sentences.en: So it's round about the time that we ended the last podcaSt. Is that right?
sentences.zh: 所以这大约是我们上一期播客结束的时间。对吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I just thought it would be interesting just to zoom in because we've been, you know, it's been a lot of kind of broad brush higher politics.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得深入了解一下会很有趣，因为我们之前谈论的都是很大范围的高层政治。

sentences.en: And I think the Horst Wessel story kind of highlights quite a lot of these broader themes.
sentences.zh: 我认为霍斯特·威塞尔的故事在很大程度上突显了这些更广泛的主题。

sentences.en: And at the end of episode two, you were talking about how the Nazis had a particular appeal for the young.
sentences.zh: 在第二集结尾，你谈到了纳粹对年轻人有着特殊的吸引力。

sentences.en: And Wessel absolutely illustrates that.
sentences.zh: 而威塞尔完全印证了这一点。

sentences.en: So you talked about Himmler, who was born in 1900, but Wessel is born in 1907.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了1900年出生的希姆莱，但威塞尔出生于1907年。

sentences.en: So he's joining the Nazi party, age 19.
sentences.zh: 所以他加入纳粹党时才19岁。

sentences.en: He is also, he's very middle class.
sentences.zh: 他也是，他非常中产阶级。

sentences.en: His father was a Lutheran pastor.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是一位路德宗牧师。

sentences.en: And essentially, I think that Wessel discovers in the Nazis, a sense of excitement and glamour and swagger and purpose that he is not finding in the church.
sentences.zh: 本质上，我认为威塞尔在纳粹身上发现了一种他在教会中找不到的兴奋感、魅力、狂傲和目标感。

sentences.en: In the previous generation, he might have done, but not now.
sentences.zh: 上一代人可能找到过，但现在不行了。

sentences.en: Like a lot of the young people that you were talking about in the previous episode, he has a feeling that he has missed out on fighting in the Great War.
sentences.zh: 就像你上一集谈到的许多年轻人一样，他有一种错过了参加那场伟大战争的感觉。

sentences.en: He was also, again, quite like, you say, Goebbels or other leading Nazis.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如你所说，他也很像戈培尔或其他纳粹高层。

sentences.en: He was not physically prepossessing as a boy.
sentences.zh: 他小时候外表并不出众。

sentences.en: He'd fallen off a horse and broken his arm.
sentences.zh: 他曾从马上摔下来摔断了胳膊。

sentences.en: And so almost by way of compensation, he was obsessed with violence.
sentences.zh: 所以几乎是为了补偿，他沉迷于暴力。

sentences.en: He kind of taught himself martial arts, practice boxing, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他自学了武术，练习拳击，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And he had this kind of, you know, going to school and then going on to university.
sentences.zh: 他有这种，你知道，上学然后上大学的经历。

sentences.en: He studies law in Berlin.
sentences.zh: 他在柏林学习法律。

sentences.en: He has this interest in street fighting.
sentences.zh: 他对街头斗殴很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And when Goebbels comes to Berlin, Berlin is a very red Berlin.
sentences.zh: 当戈培尔来到柏林时，柏林是一个非常“红色”的柏林。

sentences.en: It's a very communist city.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常共产主义的城市。

sentences.en: Goebbels recognizes in Wessel, someone who can provide him with a spear point, driving it into the guts of the, you know, the communist areas of Berlin.
sentences.zh: 戈培尔在威塞尔身上看到了一个可以为他提供矛头的人，能刺入柏林共产主义地区的核心。

sentences.en: And Wessel brings some of those kind of Lutheran qualities to it.
sentences.zh: 而威塞尔为之带来了一些路德宗的特质。

sentences.en: So that song, the horse Wessel song, it's written like a hymn.
sentences.zh: 所以那首歌，《霍斯特·威塞尔之歌》，写得就像一首赞美诗。

sentences.en: And Wessel is writing lots of these songs, and he's kind of hiring musicians, and they're marching through communist areas, playing these songs, getting into fights.
sentences.zh: 威塞尔写了很多这样的歌，他雇佣音乐家，他们穿过共产主义地区，演奏这些歌曲，并引发斗殴。

sentences.en: And Wessel ends up being shot.
sentences.zh: 最终威塞尔被枪杀了。

sentences.en: He actually kind of gets shot in the face in his own room.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是在自己的房间里被击中了面部。

sentences.en: And he kind of lingers in agony for several weeks and then dies.
sentences.zh: 他在痛苦中挣扎了几周，然后去世了。

sentences.en: And Goebbels picks on him to play the role of a martyr.
sentences.zh: 戈培尔选中他来扮演烈士的角色。

sentences.en: And I use the word advisedly because Goebbels, who comes from a Catholic background, deliberately echoes Christian iconography.
sentences.zh: 我慎重地使用了这个词，因为出身天主教背景的戈培尔，刻意呼应了基督教的肖像学。

sentences.en: He ends, you know, at the funeral service, he explicitly compares Wessel to ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 他在葬礼上明确地将威塞尔比作基督。

sentences.en: Just reading your notes.
sentences.zh: 我正在读你的笔记。

sentences.en: Extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 太不可思议了。

sentences.en: A man who calls out through his deeds, come to me, I shall redeem you.
sentences.zh: 一个通过自己的行为呼唤人们的人：到我这里来，我将救赎你们。

sentences.en: A divine element works in him, making him the man he is and causing him to act in this way.
sentences.zh: 一种神圣的元素在他身上运作，使他成为现在的他，并促使他以这种方式行事。

sentences.en: One man must set an example and offer himself up as a sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 一个人必须树立榜样，并将自己作为祭品献祭。

sentences.en: I mean, it's explicit, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很明确，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's not even...
sentences.zh: 甚至不是……

sentences.en: It's absolutely explicit.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是明确的。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, and in due course, Wessel will come to serve Nazis almost as a kind of god.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在适当的时候，威塞尔几乎成了纳粹心目中的一种神。

sentences.en: You have girls in the 30s who go to kind of, you know, woods or the ruins of amphitheaters or whatever, and make offerings to Wessel if they can't get pregnant.
sentences.zh: 在30年代，有些女孩会去树林或圆形剧场遗址等地，如果她们无法怀孕，就会向威塞尔献祭。

sentences.en: I mean, it's very, very odd.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这非常非常奇怪。

sentences.en: Incredible.
sentences.zh: 难以置信。

sentences.en: At the Nuremberg rally, they sing, we don't follow Christ, we follow Horst Wessel.
sentences.zh: 在纽伦堡集会上，他们唱道：我们不追随基督，我们追随霍斯特·威塞尔。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think that that shows the readiness of the Nazis to construct a mythology that will be appealing.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这显示了纳粹构建一种具有吸引力的神话的准备工作。

sentences.en: And I think that Wessel's own life shows that a huge part of what the Nazis offer to young men who are looking for a sense of purpose is a sense of drama, of action,
sentences.zh: 我认为威塞尔的一生表明，纳粹为那些寻找目标感的年轻人提供的大部分东西，是一种戏剧感、行动感，

sentences.en: and the kind of thrill of violence.
sentences.zh: 以及那种暴力的快感。

sentences.en: And all of this is obviously happening against the backdrop of the Great Depression, which, as conventionally told, is what helps bring the Nazis to power.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切显然都发生在大萧条的背景下，按照传统的说法，这正是帮助纳粹上台的原因。

sentences.en: And to what extent is that actually the case, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这种情况在多大程度上是真的呢？

sentences.en: Well, as your story suggests, I think, Tom, the Nazis would have always had an appeal in the kind of traumatized, brutalized, very unhappy, neurotic landscape of 1920s Germany,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，正如你的故事所暗示的那样，我认为即使经济状况好得多，纳粹在20世纪20年代德国那种受创伤、被蹂躏、非常不幸、神经质的景观中，也总是会有吸引力。

sentences.en: even if the economy had been doing much better.
sentences.zh: 即使经济状况好得多。

sentences.en: So, you know, the people, somebody like Horst Wessel doesn't fight in the war, looking for meaning, looking for belonging.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，像霍斯特·威塞尔这样的人没有参加战争，他在寻找意义，寻找归属感。

sentences.en: Christianity doesn't offer that, doesn't seem to offer that anymore.
sentences.zh: 基督教并没有提供这些，似乎也不再能提供这些了。

sentences.en: So it would have been a fringe appeal.
sentences.zh: 所以这本来只是一种边缘的吸引力。

sentences.en: But what transforms the Nazis' fortunes, I think, irrevocably, is the impact of the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，真正不可逆转地改变纳粹命运的，是大萧条的影响。

sentences.en: So Germany was always struggling in the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 德国在20世纪20年代一直处于挣扎之中。

sentences.en: It's struggling with the burden of the First World War, as Britain is, actually.
sentences.zh: 它在为第一次世界大战的负担而挣扎，实际上英国也是如此。

sentences.en: But Germany has to pay reparations.
sentences.zh: 但德国必须支付赔款。

sentences.en: But Germany has to pay reparations.
sentences.zh: 但德国必须支付赔款。

sentences.en: It's had their hyperinflation, for which there's no real British equivalent.
sentences.zh: 它经历了恶性通货膨胀，这在英国没有真正的对应物。

sentences.en: Germany has begun to recover by the second half of the 20s, but it's done so very, it's very dependent on loans from American banks.
sentences.zh: 德国在20年代下半叶开始复苏，但非常依赖美国银行的贷款。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so that makes it very, very susceptible to the crash.
sentences.zh: 这使得它非常非常容易受到崩盘的影响。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a terrible position to be in.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可怕的处境。

sentences.en: So Germany is not unusual.
sentences.zh: 所以德国并不特殊。

sentences.en: Austria is the same, a lot of Central Europe.
sentences.zh: 奥地利也是一样，中欧大部分地区也是如此。

sentences.en: It's already got quite high unemployment by 1929, by the point at which you have the Wall Street crash in October 1929, which, I mean, you know, most of our listeners, I imagine,
sentences.zh: 到1929年，也就是1929年10月华尔街崩盘时，它已经有了相当高的失业率，我想我们的大多数听众，

sentences.en: will be vaguely familiar with the stock market crashing, apocryphal stories.
sentences.zh: 应该对股市崩盘和那些传闻故事略知一二。

sentences.en: And they are apocryphal of people leaping out of the windows of Wall Street buildings and so on.
sentences.zh: 那些关于人们从华尔街大楼窗户跳下之类的故事，都是杜撰的。

sentences.en: What happens, what definitely happens, though, is that American banks start to withdraw their money from Central Europe.
sentences.zh: 然而，确实发生的事情是，美国银行开始从欧洲中部撤资。

sentences.en: And that's quite a protracted process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当漫长的过程。

sentences.en: So that takes about a year or so to really, for the full horror of the impact to become apparent.
sentences.zh: 所以大约需要一年左右的时间，这种影响的全部恐怖才会显现出来。

sentences.en: So, I mean, Horst Wessel is shot in the beginning of 1930.
sentences.zh: 所以，霍斯特·威塞尔在1930年初被枪杀。

sentences.en: And at that point, the Depression has not yet fully hit Germany.
sentences.zh: 在那时，大萧条还没有完全冲击德国。

sentences.en: It fully hits in the spring and summer of 1931.
sentences.zh: 它在1931年的春夏完全爆发。

sentences.en: So it's the collapse of the big Austrian bank, the Credit Anstalt, which I think at the time was the biggest bank in Central Europe.
sentences.zh: 那是奥地利大银行——信贷银行的倒闭，我认为当时它是中欧最大的银行。

sentences.en: And then takes lots of other banks with it.
sentences.zh: 然后它又拖垮了许多其他银行。

sentences.en: And so, again, that poor price is middle class who've had their savings with it.
sentences.zh: 所以，那些把积蓄存在那里的中产阶级又遭殃了。

sentences.en: Oh, I mean, the stats are frightening.
sentences.zh: 哦，我的意思是，这些统计数据令人恐惧。

sentences.en: So about one in three workers, registered workers, is out of work in Germany by 1932.
sentences.zh: 到1932年，德国大约每三个登记在册的工人中就有一个失业。

sentences.en: It's probably even worse in the big industrial heartlands in the Ruhr and Silesia.
sentences.zh: 在鲁尔区和西里西亚等大型工业中心，情况可能更糟。

sentences.en: I think I got this from Richard Evans' book.
sentences.zh: 我想我是从理查德·埃文斯的书中看到的。

sentences.en: About 13 million people in Germany at this point.
sentences.zh: 当时德国大约有1300万人。

sentences.en: So that's what, you know, getting on for a quarter of the population or so, slightly less, are living in households that are blighted by unemployment.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，接近四分之一的人口，或者稍微少一点，生活在受失业困扰的家庭中。

sentences.en: Where they're either dependents of people who don't have a job or they don't have a job themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们要么是失业者的家属，要么自己就没有工作。

sentences.en: You get a half a million people homeless, people turning in their droves to prostitution, to begging, to crime, and so on.
sentences.zh: 有五十万人无家可归，人们成群结队地转向卖淫、乞讨、犯罪等等。

sentences.en: And it's the criminality, isn't it, for the Nazis and indeed for the communists.
sentences.zh: 对于纳粹，实际上对于共产党人来说，这正是犯罪行为，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it kind of heightens the sense that the streets are a battleground.
sentences.zh: 这加剧了一种街道是战场的感官。

sentences.en: So Horst Vessel, somebody like him, I mean, he's been drawn into kind of paramilitary politics, which has been there since the end of the First World War in 1918.
sentences.zh: 所以霍斯特·威塞尔，像他这样的人，我的意思是，他被卷入了自1918年第一次世界大战结束以来就一直存在的准军事政治中。

sentences.en: But of course, when you have so many unemployed young men, you say to them, here's a uniform, here's a truncheon or a pistol, come into the streets, you know, join us.
sentences.zh: 但当然，当你拥有这么多失业的年轻人时，你对他们说，这里有制服，这里有警棍或手枪，到街上去，你知道，加入我们。

sentences.en: We are, I mean, that song that you, I mean, thank God you didn't sing it.
sentences.zh: 我们是，我的意思是，那首歌你，我的意思是，谢天谢地你没唱出来。

sentences.en: But it's like a kind of hyper-militarized Boy Scouts anthem.
sentences.zh: 但它就像一种高度军事化的童子军赞歌。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that's exactly what it is.
sentences.zh: 我想这正是它的本质。

sentences.en: Babylon Berlin, the TV series that we talked about, the German, brilliant German TV series we talked about in the last episode, captures this very well.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到的电视剧《巴比伦柏林》，那部我们在上一集谈到的精彩的德国电视剧，很好地捕捉到了这一点。

sentences.en: That young men who are looking for something, who are sick of the old men's world, you know, somebody gives them a belt.
sentences.zh: 那些寻找某种东西、厌倦了老人世界的年轻人，你知道，有人给了他们一条腰带。

sentences.en: Excitement.
sentences.zh: 兴奋。

sentences.en: A shirt, excitement, belonging, friends, the stormtroopers, they will go on camps and sit around the fire and sing songs and all of this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 一件衬衫，兴奋，归属感，朋友，冲锋队，他们会去露营，围坐在火堆旁唱歌，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Now, the communists are doing this too.
sentences.zh: 现在，共产党人也在这样做。

sentences.en: So communist membership trebles between 1929 and 1932.
sentences.zh: 所以共产党的人数在1929年到1932年间翻了三倍。

sentences.en: The unemployed in particular are drawn to communism.
sentences.zh: 失业者尤其被共产主义所吸引。

sentences.en: You can completely understand why.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以理解为什么。

sentences.en: The leader of the Communist Party, sort of their answer to Hitler, if you like, is a man called Ernst Tellmann, who's a manual laborer from Hamburg.
sentences.zh: 共产党领导人，如果你愿意的话，可以看作是希特勒的对应者，是一个叫恩斯特·台尔曼的人，他是汉堡的一名体力劳动者。

sentences.en: He, like Hitler, won the Iron Cross in the First World War.
sentences.zh: 他像希特勒一样，在第一次世界大战中获得了铁十字勋章。

sentences.en: He's a pure, classic communist, revolutionary StaliniSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一个纯粹的、典型的共产主义者，斯大林主义者。

sentences.en: You know, he's taking orders from Moscow.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他听命于莫斯科。

sentences.en: He absolutely believes in revolution.
sentences.zh: 他绝对相信革命。

sentences.en: He believes in smashing the bourgeois parties.
sentences.zh: 他相信粉碎资产阶级政党。

sentences.en: The communists hate the Social Democrats and the parties of Weimar.
sentences.zh: 共产党人痛恨社会民主党和魏玛的各政党。

sentences.en: Not, you know, it's understandable why.
sentences.zh: 不是，你知道，这很容易理解为什么。

sentences.en: Because the Social Democrats had used the army against them in 1918, 1919.
sentences.zh: 因为社会民主党在1918年、1919年曾动用军队对付他们。

sentences.en: And so this is key to understand, isn't it, that the Nazis are,
sentences.zh: 所以理解这一点是关键，不是吗，纳粹是，

sentences.en: so Horst Vessel is being sent in by Goebbels to rough up the communists and to provoke them and to generate street fighting against them.
sentences.zh: 所以霍斯特·威塞尔被戈培尔派去殴打共产党人，挑衅他们，并引发针对他们的街头斗殴。

sentences.en: So for Horst Vessel and Goebbels, the communists are the main adversary.
sentences.zh: 所以对于霍斯特·威塞尔和戈培尔来说，共产党人是主要的对手。

sentences.en: But for the communists, even though they don't like the Nazis, if they're given the opportunity, they'll go up to Horst Vessel's room and shoot him in the face.
sentences.zh: 但对于共产党人来说，尽管他们不喜欢纳粹，但如果有机会，他们会去霍斯特·威塞尔的房间，朝他的脸上开枪。

sentences.en: But for them, in a way, the main enemy aren't the Nazis at all.
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，对他们来说，主要的敌人根本不是纳粹。

sentences.en: It's the Social Democrats.
sentences.zh: 而是社会民主党。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a funny one, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，这很有趣，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's kind of like people on the far left of the Labour Party disliking Blairites more than they dislike Tories.
sentences.zh: 这有点像工党极左翼的人讨厌布莱尔派胜过讨厌保守党。

sentences.en: It is that.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It is that in a way, Tom.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上确实如此，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a very sort of exaggerated and lurid version of that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一种被极度夸大且耸人听闻的版本。

sentences.en: So, yes, I think the communists would say, they'd say the Nazis are just a kind of efflorescence.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我想共产党人会说，他们会说纳粹只是一种变异的产物。

sentences.en: The Nazis are just clowns and criminals.
sentences.zh: 纳粹不过是一群小丑和罪犯。

sentences.en: The real enemy are the bourgeois capitalists of the SPD and their allies, the liberals, the Catholic Center Party.
sentences.zh: 真正的敌人是德国社会民主党（SPD）的资产阶级资本家，以及他们的盟友——自由派和天主教中央党。

sentences.en: These are the people who are holding us down.
sentences.zh: 正是这些人压迫着我们。

sentences.en: These are the people for whom the police work and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 正是这些人让警察为他们效劳，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And they're the people we must smash to build a worker's state.
sentences.zh: 而他们正是我们为了建立工人国家必须粉碎的对象。

sentences.en: And this is a tension that kind of goes back to Rosa Luxemburg and everybody who, her death in 1919, the communists blame on the Social Democrats,
sentences.zh: 这种紧张关系可以追溯到罗莎·卢森堡及其1919年的遇害，共产党人将此归咎于社会民主党人，

sentences.en: but presumably gets turbocharged by the experience of the Depression.
sentences.zh: 但这种情绪大概在大萧条的经历中得到了极大的强化。

sentences.en: It does indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Absolutely does.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So, 1929, in May 1929, there's a very famous incident shown in the series Babylon Berlin called Bloody May, where the Berlin police,
sentences.zh: 所以，1929年，1929年5月，在电视剧《巴比伦柏林》中展示了一个非常著名的事件，被称为“血腥五月”，当时柏林警察，

sentences.en: who are being controlled by the Social Democrats, they attack a communist demonstration.
sentences.zh: 在社会民主党的控制下，袭击了一场共产党的示威活动。

sentences.en: They kill 33 people and injure hundreds more.
sentences.zh: 他们杀害了33人，并造成数百人受伤。

sentences.en: I mean, this for the communists is, you know, this inflames them against the Social Democrats still further.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对共产党人来说，这让他们对社会民主党的愤怒进一步加剧了。

sentences.en: Now, of course, the interesting thing is the communists hate the bourgeois parties as much as they hate the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 当然，有趣的是，共产党人憎恨资产阶级政党的程度丝毫不亚于他们对纳粹的憎恨。

sentences.en: The bourgeois parties are the people who vote for them.
sentences.zh: 资产阶级政党正是那些投票支持他们的人。

sentences.en: If they are given a choice, if they had to choose between the Nazis and the communists, they, I think, would generally choose the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 如果给他们一个选择，如果他们必须在纳粹和共产党之间做出选择，我想他们通常会选择纳粹。

sentences.en: Because the communists are going to expropriate their property, create a revolution.
sentences.zh: 因为共产党会没收他们的财产，发动革命。

sentences.en: You know, they think they're going to bring Stalinism.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们认为共产党会带来斯大林主义。

sentences.en: They look at the Nazis and they say, well, the Nazis probably talk very, you know, they're full of all this stuff and all this violence.
sentences.zh: 他们看着纳粹，心想，好吧，纳粹可能说得天花乱坠，你知道，他们充满了各种言论和暴力。

sentences.en: But actually, if they got into government, they'll probably take them.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如果他们进入政府，他们可能会接纳他们。

sentences.en: They won't nick your house.
sentences.zh: 他们不会抢走你的房子。

sentences.en: They won't confiscate your property and probably they would work with conservative elites and it would actually be fine.
sentences.zh: 他们不会没收你的财产，而且他们很可能会与保守派精英合作，一切其实都会好起来的。

sentences.en: So the effect of this, a great, great sentence in Michael Burley's book, Third Reich, New History.
sentences.zh: 所以，迈克尔·伯利在他的著作《第三帝国：一部新历史》中有一句非常精彩的话，描述了这种影响。

sentences.en: The electoral profile of the National Socialist Party has been described as an integrative people's party with an accentuated middle class character or less pretentiously as having the profile of a man with a potbelly.
sentences.zh: 国家社会主义党的选民画像被描述为一种具有突出中产阶级特征的整合型人民政党，或者用不那么自命不凡的话说，其形象就像一个大腹便便的男人。

sentences.en: All right, crikey.
sentences.zh: 好吧，天哪。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, that's absolutely, I mean, it's definitely true that even though you have the antics of people like Horse Vessel being shot in the face and street fighting,
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，这绝对是正确的，我的意思是，尽管有像霍斯特·威塞尔那样被人打中脸部以及街头斗殴的闹剧，

sentences.en: that by 1929, 1930 or so, the Nazis are beginning to win more kind of respectable votes.
sentences.zh: 但到了1929年、1930年左右，纳粹开始赢得更多所谓的体面选票。

sentences.en: Now, all of that said, the Nazis still would not have got into power, I think,
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我认为如果不是因为魏玛精英们犯下了现代史上最公然、最令人震惊的政治自杀行为，

sentences.en: had it not been for the fact that the Weimar elites commit probably the most flagrant and shocking act of political suicide in modern history.
sentences.zh: 纳粹仍然无法上台。

sentences.en: And what will follow is very complicated and intricate and involves all kinds of manoeuvring and faction fighting.
sentences.zh: 接下来的事情非常复杂和错综复杂，涉及各种操纵和派系斗争。

sentences.en: But step by step, the people who should, I mean, as we said last time,
sentences.zh: 但一步一步地，那些本应——我的意思是，正如我们上次所说，

sentences.en: the people who should be the guardians of Weimar democracy are actually digging its grave and indeed their own graves in some circumstances.
sentences.zh: 那些本应是魏玛民主守护者的人，实际上正在挖掘它的坟墓，在某些情况下，也是在挖掘他们自己的坟墓。

sentences.en: So should we get into that story, Tom?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们要开始讲那个故事了吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: It's a complicated story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个复杂的故事。

sentences.en: Are you girding your loins?
sentences.zh: 你准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, let's gird our loins for this.
sentences.zh: 是的，让我们为这个故事做好准备吧。

sentences.en: So the process by which the Weimar Republic commits suicide against this backdrop of depression, of street fighting, of red-on-brown violence and brown-on-red violence,
sentences.zh: 在这个大萧条、街头斗殴、红对棕暴力和棕对红暴力的背景下，魏玛共和国自杀的过程，

sentences.en: so terrible situation when really anyone with, you know, a concern for democracy should be manning the defences.
sentences.zh: 这是一个可怕的局面，当真正任何关心民主的人都应该守卫防线时，

sentences.en: And instead, they basically kind of demolish the walls.
sentences.zh: 他们却基本上拆毁了围墙。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: So the first blow is struck in March 1930.
sentences.zh: 所以第一击发生在1930年3月。

sentences.en: So up to this point, the government had been run by a grand coalition under a guy called Hermann Muller, who was from the Social Democrats,
sentences.zh: 在那之前，政府一直由赫尔曼·穆勒领导的大联合政府管理，他是社会民主党人，

sentences.en: and it's a coalition of the Social Democrats, the Liberal Parties and the Catholic Centre Party.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由社会民主党、自由党和天主教中央党组成的联盟。

sentences.en: But that, for various complicated reasons, which we don't need to go into, that coalition falls apart.
sentences.zh: 但由于各种复杂的原因，我们不需要深入探讨，那个联盟瓦解了。

sentences.en: And at that point, there was no majority in the Reichstag.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，国会中没有多数派。

sentences.en: Now, President Hindenburg, the World War I general, who we talked about last time, who is the-
sentences.zh: 现在，兴登堡总统，我们上次谈到的那位一战将军，他是——

sentences.en: The Prussian walrus.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士海象。

sentences.en: The Prussian walrus, as you described him.
sentences.zh: 正如你所描述的，普鲁士海象。

sentences.en: I said he was cut from oak, but you described him as a walrus.
sentences.zh: 我说他是橡木雕成的，但你把他描述成海象。

sentences.en: He's both.
sentences.zh: 他两者都是。

sentences.en: He's an oak, a wooden walrus.
sentences.zh: 他是一棵橡木，一只木头海象。

sentences.en: He and his circle have never liked democracy, never liked all the parliamentary horse trading.
sentences.zh: 他和他的圈子从来都不喜欢民主，从来都不喜欢所有的议会政治交易。

sentences.en: They distrust it.
sentences.zh: 他们不信任它。

sentences.en: They think it's un-German.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这不符合德国精神。

sentences.en: They think it's weak.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这很软弱。

sentences.en: They think it betrays the legacy of Bismarck and the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这背叛了俾斯麦和皇帝的遗产。

sentences.en: And they think this is a good chance to start building, you know, the road towards the return of a proper authoritarian regime.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是一个开始铺设通往恢复正统威权政权之路的好机会。

sentences.en: And the people in the army like this, they think, yes, because we want to rearm.
sentences.zh: 军队里的人喜欢这样，他们想，是的，因为我们想要重整军备。

sentences.en: We hate the Treaty of Versailles.
sentences.zh: 我们痛恨《凡尔赛条约》。

sentences.en: We hate having to answer to politicians.
sentences.zh: 我们痛恨不得不对政客负责。

sentences.en: You know, the more we can sort of facilitate this, the better.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们越能促进这一点越好。

sentences.en: So Hindenburg and the army generals around him, they agree that basically the answer is, stop subordinating everything to parliamentary politics.
sentences.zh: 所以兴登堡和他周围的陆军将军们一致认为，基本上答案是：停止将一切从属于议会政治。

sentences.en: Let's have a cabinet of experts.
sentences.zh: 让我们组建一个专家内阁。

sentences.en: You pick a guy from the Reichstag, and they will rule by emergency decree.
sentences.zh: 你从国会里选一个人，他们将通过紧急法令进行统治。

sentences.en: So this is the one that right from the beginning had been used.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是从一开始就被使用的那个法令。

sentences.en: Yeah, the Ebert, the Social Democrats, had used it against the left in the early 20s.
sentences.zh: 是的，艾伯特，社会民主党人，在20世纪20年代初曾用它来对付左翼。

sentences.en: It's this sort of ticking time bomb in the Weimar Constitution.
sentences.zh: 这是魏玛宪法中一颗定时炸弹。

sentences.en: I guess probably a lot of constitutions have similar emergency provisions, but the Germans have been getting used, they've got addicted to using this.
sentences.zh: 我想可能很多宪法都有类似的紧急条款，但德国人已经习惯了，他们已经对使用这种手段上瘾了。

sentences.en: Hindenburg thinks we'll rule by decree.
sentences.zh: 兴登堡认为我们将通过法令统治。

sentences.en: We won't need to worry about parliamentary majorities.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要担心议会多数派。

sentences.en: So he brings in a chap from the Catholic Center Party, the Zentrum, whose name is Heinrich Brüning.
sentences.zh: 所以他从天主教中央党（Zentrum）找来了一个人，名叫海因里希·布吕宁。

sentences.en: Brüning is from Munster.
sentences.zh: 布吕宁来自明斯特。

sentences.en: He's from a very devout Catholic family.
sentences.zh: 他来自一个非常虔诚的天主教家庭。

sentences.en: He's a very, very clever man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常非常聪明的人。

sentences.en: He's very austere, kind of bald-haired glasses.
sentences.zh: 他非常严谨，秃顶，戴着眼镜。

sentences.en: He's studied, interestingly, at Strasbourg, Bonn, and the London School of Economics, Tom.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他在斯特拉斯堡、波恩和伦敦政治经济学院学习过，汤姆。

sentences.en: And his thesis, his PhD thesis was on British railways.
sentences.zh: 他的博士论文是关于英国铁路的。

sentences.en: So, well, so clearly, clearly Germany was doomed then.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，显然，德国那时注定要完蛋了。

sentences.en: So, yes.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: So he, yet another Iron Cross winner in World War I, very patriotic, a monarchist, a believer in the Kaiser, a very sort of small C conservative man, very, very serious Catholic,
sentences.zh: 所以他，又是另一位一战铁十字勋章获得者，非常爱国，保皇党，相信皇帝，一个非常保守的人，非常非常严肃的天主教徒，

sentences.en: a tax specialiSt.
sentences.zh: 一位税务专家。

sentences.en: He's got a bit of associate of the rest is history, Antonio Salazar.
sentences.zh: 他有点像《历史的真相》节目的常客，安东尼奥·萨拉查。

sentences.en: Ah, yes.
sentences.zh: 啊，是的。

sentences.en: About him, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 关于他，我认为这样说是公平的。

sentences.en: And in fact, there's a couple of Salazarist kind of characters in this.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这里面还有几个萨拉查式的人物。

sentences.en: So he's very reactionary, in other words.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他非常反动。

sentences.en: He is pretty reactionary.
sentences.zh: 他确实相当反动。

sentences.en: His party is normally the center party, but he's pretty much on the right of that party.
sentences.zh: 他的政党通常是中央党，但他基本上处于该党的右翼。

sentences.en: He's been moving to the right anyway.
sentences.zh: 他无论如何都在向右转。

sentences.en: And he...
sentences.zh: 而且他……

sentences.en: I mean, is he as kind of, you know, back to 1450 as Salazar?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他像萨拉查那样回到1450年了吗？

sentences.en: No, he's not.
sentences.zh: 不，他没有。

sentences.en: He's not quite that bad?
sentences.zh: 他没那么糟糕？

sentences.en: No, he's not quite that bad at all.
sentences.zh: 不，他一点也不那么糟糕。

sentences.en: But he is austere.
sentences.zh: 但他很严厉。

sentences.en: His instincts are quite authoritarian.
sentences.zh: 他的本能相当威权。

sentences.en: So he starts, he restricts the freedom of the press quite early on.
sentences.zh: 所以他开始限制新闻自由，很早就开始了。

sentences.en: His economic policy is very deflationary.
sentences.zh: 他的经济政策非常紧缩。

sentences.en: So what that means is...
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着……

sentences.en: So he restricts the press.
sentences.zh: 所以他限制了新闻界。

sentences.en: Is he restricting just the left-wing press or all the press?
sentences.zh: 他限制的只是左翼媒体还是所有媒体？

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: So when...
sentences.zh: 所以当……

sentences.en: So all of Brüning's kind of law and order measures and things, they tend to be directed more at the left than the right.
sentences.zh: 所以布吕宁的所有法律和秩序措施往往更多地针对左翼而不是右翼。

sentences.en: And this is that fear of communism thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种对共产主义的恐惧。

sentences.en: This underestimation of the Nazis and the belief, very common among what you might call the sort of the respectable parliamentary parties, that the real threat is communism.
sentences.zh: 这种对纳粹的低估，以及在所谓的体面议会政党中非常普遍的信念，即真正的威胁是共产主义。

sentences.en: You can understand why they think that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你可以理解他们为什么这么想，汤姆。

sentences.en: They want to protect their property and the class system and all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们想保护自己的财产、阶级制度以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: They're also looking at what's happened in the Soviet Union and they think, Christ, that's the last thing we want to happen here.
sentences.zh: 他们也在观察苏联发生的事情，他们想，天哪，那是我们最不希望在这里发生的事情。

sentences.en: So this is understandable, but fatal.
sentences.zh: 所以这是可以理解的，但却是致命的。

sentences.en: Brüning's economic policy is very deflationary.
sentences.zh: 布吕宁的经济政策非常紧缩。

sentences.en: He doesn't believe in tax and spend.
sentences.zh: 他不相信税收和支出。

sentences.en: He doesn't believe in what we've now called Keynesianism, so public works, all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 他不相信我们现在所说的凯恩斯主义，即公共工程之类的东西。

sentences.en: He says, listen, in the midst of the depression, the thing to do is batten down the hatches, stabilize your economy, cut spending.

sentences.zh: 所以我们陷入了一场竞选活动。

sentences.en: And in the context of this bleakness, unemployment, people with nothing to do, a party that puts on a show and is promising national renewal, you can see why…

sentences.zh: 体制让你们失望了。

sentences.zh: 那些老牌政客，简直是占着茅坑不拉屎。

sentences.zh: 而我们提供的是终结阶级政治。

sentences.zh: 民族团结，一个团结一致、为伟大而奋斗的种族共同体。

sentences.zh: 他们有铜管乐队。

sentences.en: They have parades pumping the stuff out.

sentences.en: And clearly a lot of people, it's what they want to hear.
sentences.zh: 显然很多人，这正是他们想听到的。

sentences.zh: 所以就有了选举结果。

sentences.zh: 这对魏玛体制是一个沉重的打击。

sentences.zh: 这并不是因为社会民主党或天主教中央党失去了选票。

sentences.zh: 他们基本保持原样。

sentences.en: It's that the established, mainstream, respectable, conservative parties.
sentences.zh: 而是那些老牌的、主流的、体面的、保守的政党。

sentences.zh: 那些资产阶级政党。

sentences.zh: 它们几乎被彻底消灭了。

sentences.zh: 共产党的席位从54席增加到77席。

sentences.zh: 但最大的赢家是纳粹党。

sentences.zh: 比上次增加了一百万张选票。

sentences.en: Fringe party.
sentences.zh: 边缘政党。

sentences.zh: 他们现在拥有六百五十万张选票。

sentences.zh: 他们的席位从12席增加到107席。

sentences.en: They're not, they're now beginning to win many more kind of respectable, sort of, Michael

sentences.zh: 所以教师、新教牧师，你知道，那些把他们视为对抗共产主义解药的人。

sentences.en: So they're a social protest party.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是一个社会抗议政党。

sentences.en: So this is a terrible, terrible result for Weimar.
sentences.zh: 所以这对魏玛来说是一个极其糟糕的结果。

sentences.zh: 你有更多的，你有77名痛恨魏玛共和国的共产党人坐在

sentences.zh: 纳粹采取的投票箱和街头暴力双重策略现在基本上达成了一致。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 所以暴力已经被引入了魏玛共和国、魏玛体制的核心。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.zh: 而此时的魏玛体制，我认为你可以争论，它此时已经死了吗？

sentences.zh: 休息后请继续收听魏玛之死。

sentences.en: Hello, welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎回到《历史的余味》。

sentences.en: We promised you before the break, the death of Weimar.
sentences.zh: 我们休息前承诺过，魏玛之死。

sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我的意思是，魏玛死于它自诞生以来一直纠缠不清的政治并发症，这有一种极其悲剧的意味。

sentences.zh: 这就是21世纪，当然是在2010年代和2020年代，人们开始纠结的问题，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 在一个民主国家，你该如何对待一个参与竞争、作为参赛者，但决心摧毁他们所参与的游戏本身的人？

sentences.en: How do you exclude them?
sentences.zh: 你如何排除他们？

sentences.en: How do you control them?
sentences.zh: 你如何控制他们？

sentences.en: Do you try to tame them?
sentences.zh: 你是试图驯服他们吗？

sentences.en: Do you work with them?
sentences.zh: 你是与他们合作吗？

sentences.en: Would you just say never?
sentences.zh: 还是你会说绝不？

sentences.en: So this is the problem that is facing the...
sentences.zh: 所以这就是面临的问题……

sentences.zh: 这非常《每日电讯报》，不是吗？

sentences.en: Very Daily Telegraph.
sentences.zh: 非常《每日电讯报》。

sentences.en: But it's absolutely not Germany's priority in 1932.
sentences.zh: 但这绝对不是1932年德国的当务之急。

sentences.en: Papen and Schleicher, so they team up for the time being.
sentences.zh: 帕彭和施莱谢尔，他们暂时联手了。

sentences.en: The intriguing general and the intriguing effete...
sentences.zh: 那个搞阴谋的将军和那个搞阴谋的虚弱的……

sentences.en: What was he in an effete?
sentences.zh: 他怎么就虚弱了？

sentences.en: Machiavelli.
sentences.zh: 马基雅维利主义者。

sentences.en: Well, yet again, they persuade President Hindenburg to dissolve the Reichstag and call new elections.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们又一次说服了兴登堡总统解散国会并举行新的选举。

sentences.en: I mean, why people keep on doing this?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么人们总是不断地这样做？

sentences.en: This is a great error.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的错误。

sentences.en: I mean, even though...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使……

sentences.en: Oh, because that's the definition of...
sentences.zh: 哦，因为这就是……的定义。

sentences.en: Famously, the definition of insanity is keep repeating the same mistake over and over again, expecting it to come out differently.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，疯狂的定义就是不断重复同样的错误，却期望得到不同的结果。

sentences.en: It's strange when you read the accounts, especially by kind of, you know, sort of left-leaning historians like Richard Evans, who keep saying, they keep basically saying,
sentences.zh: 当你阅读这些记录时，尤其是像理查德·埃文斯这样倾向左翼的历史学家所写的记录时，会觉得很奇怪，他们一直在说，他们基本上一直在问，

sentences.en: why do they not just prorogue the parliament forever and impose some kind of authoritarian rule?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们不干脆永远解散议会，实施某种威权统治呢？

sentences.en: Why do they keep making these terrible mistakes?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们总是犯这些可怕的错误？

sentences.en: Anyway, they do this.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: Because presumably, the alternatives, as we now see, is a kind of authoritarian military dictatorship, or the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 因为大概，正如我们现在所见，其他的选择要么是某种威权军事独裁，要么是纳粹。

sentences.en: And because we know which is the worst of those, we're tempted to see it as the worst of all fates.
sentences.zh: 而且因为我们知道哪一个更糟，所以我们倾向于将其视为最糟糕的命运。

sentences.en: But they, you know, to repeat, they don't know that, do they?
sentences.zh: 但他们，你知道，再说一遍，他们并不知道这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: You're right, of course.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，当然。

sentences.en: But they're also...
sentences.zh: 但他们也……

sentences.en: I mean, they do want a military dictatorship, but they're kind of frightened that they won't get to do it themselves, that somebody else will take it over.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们确实想要军事独裁，但他们有点害怕自己无法亲自掌控，会被别人夺走。

sentences.en: They're also frightened of alarming the public and provoking civil war.
sentences.zh: 他们也害怕惊动公众并引发内战。

sentences.en: So they want to get...
sentences.zh: 所以他们想……

sentences.en: They want to put themselves in a position where nobody...
sentences.zh: 他们想把自己置于一个没有人……的位置。

sentences.en: There won't be anybody in the street complaining, where everybody would be delighted, where they've got maybe backing the Reichstag for it.
sentences.zh: 街上不会有人抱怨，每个人都会很高兴，也许还能得到国会的支持。

sentences.en: They call new elections.
sentences.zh: 他们宣布举行新的选举。

sentences.en: They think...
sentences.zh: 他们认为……

sentences.en: They're conscious of Hitler and his strength, and they think to themselves, listen, we don't want to really alienate him.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到希特勒及其势力，他们心想，听着，我们不想真的疏远他。

sentences.en: So they lift...
sentences.zh: 所以他们解除了……

sentences.en: There's been a ban on the stormtroopers marching openly.
sentences.zh: 之前一直有禁令，禁止冲锋队公开游行。

sentences.en: They say, we'll lift this ban, because this will appease him, buy him off, and maybe make him an ally.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们要解除这项禁令，因为这能安抚他，收买他，或许还能让他成为盟友。

sentences.en: What could possibly go wrong?
sentences.zh: 能出什么岔子呢？

sentences.en: What could possibly go wrong?
sentences.zh: 能出什么岔子呢？

sentences.en: Well, almost immediately in July 1932, there's enormous fighting in a place called Altona in Prussia, which is near Hamburg,
sentences.zh: 好吧，几乎就在1932年7月，普鲁士一个叫阿尔托纳的地方发生了大规模冲突，那地方离汉堡很近，

sentences.en: between the stormtroopers and the communist Red Front.
sentences.zh: 发生在冲锋队和共产党“红色阵线”之间。

sentences.en: And 18 people are killed and hundreds of people are injured because the police lose control and they start shooting wildly.
sentences.zh: 造成了18人死亡，数百人受伤，因为警方失去了控制，开始疯狂开火。

sentences.en: And Papen then makes another of these terrible, terrible mistakes.
sentences.zh: 帕彭随后又犯下了另一个极其严重的错误。

sentences.en: Instead of doing what he should have done, which is to ban all the paramilitaries completely, he thinks, great,
sentences.zh: 他本该做的是彻底取缔所有准军事组织，但他却觉得，太好了，

sentences.en: I can use this as an opportunity to seize control of the state government of Prussia.
sentences.zh: 我可以借此机会夺取普鲁士州政府的控制权。

sentences.en: So Prussia is by far...
sentences.zh: 普鲁士可是……

sentences.en: Prussia is the England of Germany.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士就是德国的英格兰。

sentences.en: It dominates Germany.
sentences.zh: 它主宰着德国。

sentences.en: It's by far the biggest state.
sentences.zh: 它是德国最大的州，遥遥领先。

sentences.en: If you control Prussia, you don't quite control the lot, but you're a lot of the way there.
sentences.zh: 如果你控制了普鲁士，虽然还没完全控制整个国家，但也差不多了。

sentences.en: And Prussia is run by the Social Democrats.
sentences.zh: 而普鲁士是由社会民主党人管理的。

sentences.en: And basically, von Papen and Hindenburg dissolve by emergency decree the Social Democratic...
sentences.zh: 基本上，冯·帕彭和兴登堡通过紧急法令解散了社会民主党……

sentences.en: They take over the Social Democratic government of Prussia.
sentences.zh: 他们接管了普鲁士的社会民主党政府。

sentences.en: They kick out the Social Democrats from their great stronghold.
sentences.zh: 他们把社会民主党人从他们的大本营里踢了出去。

sentences.en: And von Papen will use this as his own personal fiefdom.
sentences.zh: 冯·帕彭将把这里当作自己的私人领地。

sentences.en: And this is a disaster for democracy, because here you have the central government, unconstitutionally effectively, getting rid of the biggest party.
sentences.zh: 这对民主来说是一场灾难，因为中央政府在实际上违宪地除掉了最大的政党。

sentences.en: And the Social Democrats do nothing to resist it.
sentences.zh: 而社会民主党人对此毫无抵抗。

sentences.en: Why do they not resist it?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么不反抗？

sentences.en: Because they're worried about civil war as well?
sentences.zh: 是因为他们也担心内战吗？

sentences.en: They are, exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: The Social Democrats are paralysed.
sentences.zh: 社会民主党人瘫痪了。

sentences.en: But they've been paralysed the whole way through, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 但他们一直以来不都是瘫痪的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, they've been kind of sitting there waiting for the revolution to come and nothing ever happens.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们一直坐在那里等着革命到来，结果什么也没发生。

sentences.en: It's that, but also they've known from the very beginning of Weimar that lots of people in the army don't like them.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他们从魏玛共和国建立之初就知道，军队里很多人不喜欢他们。

sentences.en: And that there are lots of reactionaries who think they're illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多反动派认为他们是非法的。

sentences.en: I mean, they've known this from even before the First World War.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们甚至在第一次世界大战前就知道这一点。

sentences.en: And at this key moment, they do nothing.
sentences.zh: 而在如此关键的时刻，他们却什么也没做。

sentences.en: They don't have a general strike.
sentences.zh: 他们没有发动大罢工。

sentences.en: They're being robbed of their heartland.
sentences.zh: 他们的大本营正被夺走。

sentences.en: You know, I'm trying to imagine an analogous situation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在试着想象一个类似的处境。

sentences.en: It's as though there was an elected English government that the Westminster Parliament suddenly kicked out and said,
sentences.zh: 就好像有一个民选的英国政府被威斯敏斯特议会突然踢开，然后说，

sentences.en: we'll run it ourselves, you know, in a context of street violence.
sentences.zh: 在街头暴力的背景下，我们要自己来管理它。

sentences.en: And that government did nothing about it.
sentences.zh: 而那个政府对此毫无作为。

sentences.en: It didn't say, oi, you know, that this is illegal.
sentences.zh: 它甚至没说，喂，这是违法的。

sentences.en: Take to the streets.
sentences.zh: 走上街头吧。

sentences.en: Have a general strike or something.
sentences.zh: 发动大罢工之类的。

sentences.en: So they can't have a general strike because unemployment is so high that, you know, people aren't going to down tools to go out on the streets.
sentences.zh: 他们无法发动大罢工，因为失业率太高了，人们不会放下工具走上街头。

sentences.en: So as Richard Evans says, Papen's coup dealt a mortal blow to the Weimar Republic.
sentences.zh: 正如理查德·埃文斯所说，帕彭的政变给魏玛共和国带来了致命一击。

sentences.en: It destroyed the federal principle and opened the way to the wholesale centralization of the state.
sentences.zh: 它摧毁了联邦原则，为国家权力的全面集权铺平了道路。

sentences.en: Which the Nazis are all about, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这正是纳粹所追求的。

sentences.en: Because if you have a Fuhrer.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你有一个元首。

sentences.en: So if the Nazis ever do take power, they can follow that precedent.
sentences.zh: 所以如果纳粹真的夺取了政权，他们就可以效仿这个先例。

sentences.en: So the election.
sentences.zh: 关于选举。

sentences.en: This election in July 1932 that von Papen has called takes place in a context of where we began with horse vessel and the street violence.
sentences.zh: 冯·帕彭宣布的这次1932年7月的选举，是在我们开头提到的霍斯特·威塞尔和街头暴力的背景下进行的。

sentences.en: This is now worse than ever before.
sentences.zh: 现在的情况比以往任何时候都要糟糕。

sentences.en: So Hitler is again flying around addressing different venues.
sentences.zh: 希特勒又在四处奔走，在不同的场地发表演讲。

sentences.en: The propaganda is more aggressive than ever.
sentences.zh: 宣传比以往任何时候都更具侵略性。

sentences.en: I mean, Richard Evans is brilliant on this, actually.
sentences.zh: 说真的，理查德·埃文斯对此的分析非常精彩。

sentences.en: He says, every poster, no matter what party it's for, basically looks the same.
sentences.zh: 他说，每一张海报，无论属于哪个党派，看起来基本都一样。

sentences.en: It's a giant, half-naked male worker smashing his adversaries.
sentences.zh: 都是一个巨大的、半裸的男性工人在痛击他的对手。

sentences.en: He says, all over Germany, electors were confronted with violent images of giant workers smashing their opponents to pieces, kicking them aside, yanking them out of parliament,
sentences.zh: 他说，在德国各地，选民们面对的都是暴力图像：巨大的工人在将对手撕成碎片、踢到一边、从议会里拽出来，

sentences.en: or looming over frock-coated and top-hatted politicians who were almost universally portrayed as insignificant and quarrelsome pygmies.
sentences.zh: 或者俯视着那些穿着礼服、戴着高帽的政客，这些人几乎被普遍描绘成微不足道且好斗的侏儒。

sentences.en: And, of course, if everybody's doing that, it plays into the hands of the people who do it beSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果每个人都这么做，那就正中那些最擅长此道的人的下怀。

sentences.en: Of course, yeah.
sentences.zh: 当然，没错。

sentences.en: And that's the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 那就是纳粹。

sentences.en: So they run, yet again, they say.
sentences.zh: 所以他们再次参选，他们说。

sentences.en: And the Nazis are saying, what is their policy?
sentences.zh: 纳粹在说，他们的政策是什么？

sentences.en: What is their policy to their political opponents?
sentences.zh: 他们对政治对手的政策是什么？

sentences.en: Are they saying, we'll put them in concentration camps?
sentences.zh: 他们是说，要把他们关进集中营吗？

sentences.en: We'll ban them?
sentences.zh: 我们要取缔他们吗？

sentences.en: Are they avert about that?
sentences.zh: 他们对此直言不讳吗？

sentences.en: They're never so explicit.
sentences.zh: 他们从不那么明确。

sentences.en: They're never so explicit.
sentences.zh: 他们从不那么明确。

sentences.en: They talk in abstractions.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论的是抽象概念。

sentences.en: They say, we'll end the parliamentary pygmies and their bickering.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们要终结议会侏儒及其争吵。

sentences.en: National unity.
sentences.zh: 民族团结。

sentences.en: National rebirth.
sentences.zh: 民族复兴。

sentences.en: Down with the Jewish financiers.
sentences.zh: 打倒犹太金融家。

sentences.en: Down with the communists.
sentences.zh: 打倒共产党人。

sentences.en: Down with the November criminals.
sentences.zh: 打倒十一月罪人。

sentences.en: Right, but when they say down with the communists, what are they saying they're going to do to the communists?
sentences.zh: 对，但当他们说打倒共产党人时，他们说要对共产党人做什么？

sentences.en: They're not specific.
sentences.zh: 他们没有具体说明。

sentences.en: They're never specific.
sentences.zh: 他们从不具体说明。

sentences.en: So even if you read Mein Kampf, Tom, I mean, Hitler is all generalities.
sentences.zh: 所以即使你读了《我的奋斗》，汤姆，希特勒说的全是空话。

sentences.en: It's all kind of the medical language that we've talked about a lot in this series.
sentences.zh: 全是我们在本系列中讨论过很多的那种医学语言。

sentences.en: All the sort of slightly religious language that you are obviously familiar with from your stuff with Horse Vessel.
sentences.zh: 还有那种你从霍斯特·威塞尔的相关资料中显然很熟悉的宗教色彩语言。

sentences.en: You know, that sort of talk of the talk of rebirth and national salvation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种关于重生和民族拯救的谈话。

sentences.en: It's all that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 全是那一套。

sentences.en: And that election, 31st of July, it is an absolute disaster for the mainstream and a victory for the extremes.
sentences.zh: 而那场7月31日的选举，对主流政党来说是一场彻底的灾难，对极端势力来说则是一场胜利。

sentences.en: So the Nazis double their vote, 6 to 13 million.
sentences.zh: 纳粹的得票率翻了一番，从600万增加到1300万。

sentences.en: They're now by far the biggest single party in the Reichstag, 230 seats.
sentences.zh: 他们现在是国会中遥遥领先的第一大党，拥有230个席位。

sentences.en: The communists also increased their vote.
sentences.zh: 共产党人的得票率也有所增加。

sentences.en: They're on 89 seats.
sentences.zh: 他们获得了89个席位。

sentences.en: There is a sense, however, this is as good as it will ever get for the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 然而，有一种感觉是，这对纳粹来说已经是极限了。

sentences.en: You know, this was their greater population.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是他们能争取到的最大群体了。

sentences.en: They've hit the glass ceiling.
sentences.zh: 他们触到了天花板。

sentences.en: They've probably hit a ceiling.
sentences.zh: 他们可能已经触到了天花板。

sentences.en: So even Goebbels in his diary says, you know, we've got 37% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 所以连戈培尔在日记里也说，我们获得了37%的选票。

sentences.en: It's probable we've got as many people who will ever vote for us in a kind of free election.
sentences.zh: 在某种自由选举中，这可能就是我们能获得的所有选票了。

sentences.en: So this is the point at which we should become a party of power.
sentences.zh: 所以现在是我们成为执政党的时候了。

sentences.en: We should enter government.
sentences.zh: 我们应该进入政府。

sentences.en: The issue is that they don't want to enter government as anybody else's partner.
sentences.zh: 问题是，他们不想作为任何人的伙伴进入政府。

sentences.en: Well, because Hitler can't, can he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为希特勒不能这样做，对吧？

sentences.en: No, you're right.
sentences.zh: 不，你说得对。

sentences.en: He's proclaiming himself the Fuhrer, this man of destiny, this kind of Wagnerian hero.
sentences.zh: 他自诩为元首，是天选之人，是那种瓦格纳式的英雄。

sentences.en: He can't sit down with all the frock-coated pygmies and behave like any other politician.
sentences.zh: 他不能和那些穿着礼服的侏儒坐在一起，像其他政客一样行事。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I think you're absolutely right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得你说得太对了。

sentences.en: I think if he's got this sacred destiny to lead Germany into a national revolution, how can you do that if you're sitting with the very people?
sentences.zh: 我想如果他肩负着带领德国进行民族革命的神圣使命，怎么能和这些人同流合污呢？

sentences.en: So he starts to have secret talks with General Schleicher about doing a deal and becoming chancellor.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始与施莱谢尔将军秘密会谈，试图达成协议并出任总理。

sentences.en: But for various reasons, this is in August 1932.
sentences.zh: 但由于各种原因，那是在1932年8月。

sentences.en: For various reasons, those talks run aground.
sentences.zh: 由于各种原因，这些会谈搁浅了。

sentences.en: One reason is that there's yet more extreme street violence.
sentences.zh: 其中一个原因是街头暴力变得更加极端。

sentences.en: Papen has just announced the death penalty for all political crimes.
sentences.zh: 帕彭刚刚宣布对所有政治犯罪处以死刑。

sentences.en: Basically, to use the communists.
sentences.zh: 基本上，是为了对付共产党人。

sentences.en: With an axe.
sentences.zh: 用斧头。

sentences.en: Presumably with an old-fashioned.
sentences.zh: 大概是用那种老式的。

sentences.en: Prussian axe.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士斧头。

sentences.en: So that's something to cheer the traditionalists up.
sentences.zh: 这倒是能让传统派高兴一下。

sentences.en: But just, yeah, the letter writers to the Daily Telegraph will be delighted with that.
sentences.zh: 但只是，是的，那些给《每日电讯报》写信的人会对此感到高兴的。

sentences.en: Papen wants this, he tends to use this against the communists.
sentences.zh: 帕彭想要这个，他倾向于用它来对付共产党人。

sentences.en: However, the first crime that happens within hours of the law being passed is a load of Nazi brown shirts killing a communist in an upper Silesian village.
sentences.zh: 然而，法律通过后几小时内发生的第一起罪行，是一群纳粹冲锋队员在上西里西亚的一个村庄杀害了一名共产党人。

sentences.en: And five of them are sentenced to death.
sentences.zh: 其中五人被判处死刑。

sentences.en: Hitler goes absolutely mad and says, how can you work with the, how can I work with anybody who sentences our people to death?
sentences.zh: 希特勒彻底疯了，他说，你怎么能和那些判我们的人死刑的人共事？

sentences.en: They're not criminals.
sentences.zh: 他们不是罪犯。

sentences.en: They're fighting for the fatherland.
sentences.zh: 他们是在为祖国而战。

sentences.en: Against this background, Hindenburg.
sentences.zh: 在这种背景下，兴登堡。

sentences.en: Hindenburg still has slightly cold feet about dealing with it.
sentences.zh: 兴登堡对处理这件事仍然有些退缩。

sentences.en: I mean, Hindenburg is, what did I say?
sentences.zh: 我是说，兴登堡，我刚才怎么说的？

sentences.en: Last time he was 84.
sentences.zh: 上次他说他84岁了。

sentences.en: Now he's, I mean, he's 85.
sentences.zh: 现在他，我是说，他85岁了。

sentences.en: Going on 127.
sentences.zh: 快127岁了。

sentences.en: He's still a bit iffy about this.
sentences.zh: 他对此仍然有些犹豫。

sentences.en: He has a key meeting on the 13th of August, 1932, with Hitler, the presidential palace.
sentences.zh: 1932年8月13日，他在总统府与希特勒进行了一次关键会谈。

sentences.en: He says, I want you to serve under Franz von Papen.
sentences.zh: 他说，我希望你在弗朗茨·冯·帕彭手下任职。

sentences.en: Hitler says, no, no, no, I want to be chancellor.
sentences.zh: 希特勒说，不，不，不，我要当总理。

sentences.en: I have to be chancellor.
sentences.zh: 我必须当总理。

sentences.en: I'm leading the biggest party.
sentences.zh: 我领导着最大的政党。

sentences.en: And Hindenburg says, no.
sentences.zh: 兴登堡说，不行。

sentences.en: And he says something which, you know, he should say.
sentences.zh: 他说了一些他本该说的话。

sentences.en: He says, I will not hand over the Reich to one party that is so intolerant and that encourages violence.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不会把国家交给一个如此不宽容且鼓励暴力的政党。

sentences.en: I will not do it.
sentences.zh: 我不会这么做。

sentences.en: And the meeting lasts just 20 minutes.
sentences.zh: 会谈只持续了20分钟。

sentences.en: And Hitler goes out.
sentences.zh: 希特勒走了出来。

sentences.en: Furious that Hindenburg has said no.
sentences.zh: 因为兴登堡拒绝了他而暴跳如雷。

sentences.en: That meeting is largely forgotten today.
sentences.zh: 那次会谈在今天几乎被遗忘了。

sentences.en: In his biography, Ian Kershaw says, that should have been that yet again.
sentences.zh: 伊恩·克肖在传记中说，那本该是希特勒的最后机会。

sentences.en: That was Hitler's chance and it was gone.
sentences.zh: 那是希特勒的机会，但已经错过了。

sentences.en: Is that when Hitler plunges into his big depression?
sentences.zh: 那是希特勒陷入严重抑郁的时候吗？

sentences.en: I think, well, yeah, I guess he does plunge into a big depression then.
sentences.zh: 我想，嗯，是的，我想他当时确实陷入了严重的抑郁。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because he feels he's had his chance and it slipped through his fingers.
sentences.zh: 因为他觉得自己的机会溜走了。

sentences.en: And it's, and yeah, and he's blown it.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，他搞砸了。

sentences.en: Well, it's not that he's blown it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不是他搞砸了。

sentences.en: It's that the one man that he couldn't circumvent, the war hero, the one man who really is, you know, the guardian of the constitution.
sentences.zh: 而是他无法绕过的那个人，那位战争英雄，那个真正守护宪法的人。

sentences.en: If he can't persuade Hindenburg to give him a chance, he has no hope, unless he sort of kills Hindenburg or something.
sentences.zh: 如果他不能说服兴登堡给他一个机会，他就没有希望了，除非他杀了兴登堡之类的。

sentences.en: Or Hindenburg waits till he's dead.
sentences.zh: 或者兴登堡等到他去世为止。

sentences.en: But if he waits till he's dead, Germany will have recovered from the depression by then or be in the recovery.
sentences.zh: 但如果他等到去世，到那时德国可能已经从大萧条中恢复过来，或者正在复苏中。

sentences.en: And the Nazis' momentum will have passed.
sentences.zh: 而纳粹党的势头也已经过去了。

sentences.en: So that should be that for Hitler.
sentences.zh: 所以希特勒的事就该到此为止了。

sentences.en: But of course it isn't.
sentences.zh: 但当然，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: So what happens next is pure intrigue.
sentences.zh: 所以接下来发生的事情纯粹是阴谋诡计。

sentences.en: So Papen has a plan that he will, let's just dissolve the Reichstag forever.
sentences.zh: 帕彭有个计划，他想，干脆永远解散国会算了。

sentences.en: Let's just get rid and use Hindenburg's presidential emergency powers to rule by decree.
sentences.zh: 干脆摆脱掉它，利用兴登堡的总统紧急权力进行法令统治。

sentences.en: And that will pave the way for an authoritarian regime that we've always dreamed of, that we've wanted since 1918.
sentences.zh: 那将为我们一直梦想的、自1918年以来一直渴望的威权政体铺平道路。

sentences.en: There's an incredible moment.
sentences.zh: 那是一个令人难以置信的时刻。

sentences.en: It's pure parliamentary drama.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是议会闹剧。

sentences.en: Von Papen goes to the Reichstag on the 12th of September 1932 to dissolve it, to basically set this in train.
sentences.zh: 冯·帕彭于1932年9月12日前往国会解散它，基本上是为了启动这个进程。

sentences.en: But before he can do that, the communists place a vote of no confidence in the government.
sentences.zh: 但在他能做到这一点之前，共产党人对政府提出了不信任投票。

sentences.en: And to von Papen's horror and fury, the Nazis, the biggest party who are basically running it, so Goering is the sort of president of the session,
sentences.zh: 令冯·帕彭惊恐和愤怒的是，纳粹党，这个基本上在操纵国会的最大党派——戈林算是会议主席——

sentences.en: Goering says, we'll vote on the no confidence thing firSt.
sentences.zh: 戈林说，我们先对不信任动议进行投票。

sentences.en: They vote on it, and the no confidence wins by 512 votes to 42.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了投票，结果不信任动议以512票对42票获得通过。

sentences.en: So Papen and his government are completely...
sentences.zh: 所以帕彭和他的政府完全……

sentences.en: That's a ringing defeat, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是一次惨败，不是吗？

sentences.en: A very ringing defeat.
sentences.zh: 非常惨痛的失败。

sentences.en: They're completely humiliated.
sentences.zh: 他们彻底丢尽了脸。

sentences.en: How can you now dissolve it and rule by decree when you've been so completely rebuked and shown that you have no democratic legitimacy at all?
sentences.zh: 当你受到如此彻底的斥责，并被证明完全没有民主合法性时，你现在怎么还能解散国会并进行法令统治呢？

sentences.en: And so Papen and co, they kind of lose their bottle.
sentences.zh: 所以帕彭和他的同伙，他们有点胆怯了。

sentences.en: And yet again, they say, well, we'll have another election.
sentences.zh: 他们又一次说，好吧，我们再举行一次选举。

sentences.en: Oh, I'll bang my head against this door again.
sentences.zh: 哦，我又要对着这扇门撞头了。

sentences.en: Everybody is sick of elections by now.
sentences.zh: 现在每个人都厌倦了选举。

sentences.en: Actually, the Nazis now are beginning to drop.
sentences.zh: 事实上，纳粹党的得票率现在开始下降了。

sentences.en: This is the incredible thing, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这就是令人难以置信的地方，汤姆。

sentences.en: The Nazis took power after they were dropping.
sentences.zh: 纳粹党是在他们走下坡路之后才夺取政权的。

sentences.en: Their vote drops from 13.7 million votes to 12.7 million.
sentences.zh: 他们的选票从1370万张下降到1270万张。

sentences.en: They lose 44 seats.
sentences.zh: 他们失去了44个席位。

sentences.en: They are still the biggest party, but now they are smaller than the Social Democrats and the Communists combined.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然是最大的党派，但现在他们比社会民主党和共产党加起来还要小。

sentences.en: The Communists are going up all the time.
sentences.zh: 共产党人的势力一直在上升。

sentences.en: By the way, they're now up to 100.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他们现在已经达到100席了。

sentences.en: But the Communists and the Social Democrats won't work with each other.
sentences.zh: 但共产党和社会民主党不愿合作。

sentences.en: Never work together.
sentences.zh: 永远不会合作。

sentences.en: They hate each other.
sentences.zh: 他们互相憎恨。

sentences.en: More than they hate the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 比他们憎恨纳粹还要深。

sentences.en: Well, is it more than they hate the Nazis?
sentences.zh: 嗯，真的比他们憎恨纳粹还要深吗？

sentences.en: As much as.
sentences.zh: 程度相当。

sentences.en: I think it's certainly fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我认为这样说绝对公平。

sentences.en: So what happens now?
sentences.zh: 那么现在会发生什么？

sentences.en: Total stasis.
sentences.zh: 彻底的停滞。

sentences.en: Nobody knows.
sentences.zh: 没人知道。

sentences.en: And just pure factionalism.
sentences.zh: 纯粹的派系斗争。

sentences.en: So Papen and Schleicher.
sentences.zh: 所以帕彭和施莱谢尔。

sentences.en: So the Effete Machiavelle and the intriguing general.
sentences.zh: 那个虚弱的马基雅维利和那个阴谋家将军。

sentences.en: They've kind of fallen out with each other.
sentences.zh: 他们之间闹翻了。

sentences.en: They both want to be running Germany.
sentences.zh: 他们都想统治德国。

sentences.en: They're more interested, basically, in their own personal fortunes than they are in thinking about what the Nazis truly represent.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上更关心自己的个人前途，而不是去思考纳粹真正代表了什么。

sentences.en: Schleicher says to Papen, you've got to go, mate.
sentences.zh: 施莱谢尔对帕彭说，你得走人了，伙计。

sentences.en: The army's not going to back you anymore.
sentences.zh: 军队不会再支持你了。

sentences.en: So Papen resigns.
sentences.zh: 于是帕彭辞职了。

sentences.en: There's then two weeks of sort of general intrigue.
sentences.zh: 随后有两周左右的各种阴谋活动。

sentences.en: Finally, Schleicher, the general, takes on the chancellorship himself.
sentences.zh: 最后，将军施莱谢尔亲自担任了总理。

sentences.en: It's not really what he wanted.
sentences.zh: 这其实不是他想要的。

sentences.en: I think he wanted a puppet to do it for him.
sentences.zh: 我想他想要一个傀儡来替他干活。

sentences.en: Hindenburg, by now, is very distrustful of General Schleicher.
sentences.zh: 此时的兴登堡对施莱谢尔将军非常不信任。

sentences.en: He thinks General Schleicher's been plotting against Papen all this time.
sentences.zh: 他认为施莱谢尔将军一直都在密谋反对帕彭。

sentences.en: Schleicher opens talks with the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 施莱谢尔开始与纳粹党进行谈判。

sentences.en: He appeals to Hitler's, I suppose you could say almost Hitler's rival within the Nazi party, Gregor Strasse, who's tempted.
sentences.zh: 他向希特勒的——我想你可以说是希特勒在纳粹党内的竞争对手——格雷戈尔·斯特拉瑟寻求支持，后者动心了。

sentences.en: Such a dangerous thing to be.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常危险的身份。

sentences.en: Very dangerous thing to be, as Gregor Strasse will discover.
sentences.zh: 正如格雷戈尔·斯特拉瑟后来发现的那样，那是非常危险的身份。

sentences.en: Strasse was tempted, but the Nazis say, no, you can't do this without Hitler.
sentences.zh: 斯特拉瑟动心了，但纳粹党说，不，没有希特勒你不能这么做。

sentences.en: So he ends up resigning all his posts and leaving the Nazi party.
sentences.zh: 所以他最终辞去了所有职务并离开了纳粹党。

sentences.en: Inside the Hindenburg circle, there are all talks the whole time.
sentences.zh: 在兴登堡的圈子里，一直都在进行各种谈话。

sentences.en: What on earth are we going to do?
sentences.zh: 我们到底该怎么办？

sentences.en: Who's going to run the country?
sentences.zh: 谁来管理这个国家？

sentences.en: And there are lots of conservatives around Hindenburg who say, you can't trust General Schleicher.
sentences.zh: 兴登堡周围有很多保守派说，你不能相信施莱谢尔将军。

sentences.en: You know, von Papen was quite good.
sentences.zh: 你知道，冯·帕彭其实挺不错的。

sentences.en: Get him back.
sentences.zh: 让他回来吧。

sentences.en: You know, more of the stuff with the axe.
sentences.zh: 你知道，多用点那种强硬手段。

sentences.en: Bring, I mean, he's conservative.
sentences.zh: 带他回来，我的意思是，他是保守派。

sentences.en: We can trust him.
sentences.zh: 我们可以信任他。

sentences.en: We can work with him.
sentences.zh: 我们可以和他共事。

sentences.en: They never think, why don't we bring the Kaiser back?
sentences.zh: 他们从来没想过，为什么我们不把德皇请回来？

sentences.en: No, I think the Kaiser is completely...
sentences.zh: 不，我认为德皇已经完全……

sentences.en: So he's off in Holland, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他躲在荷兰，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's off in Holland, becoming very anti-Semitic.
sentences.zh: 他躲在荷兰，变得非常反犹太。

sentences.en: So Kaiser, who previously, in his previous appearances and the rest is history, has been very much a comic figure.
sentences.zh: 所以德皇，在之前的出场和“历史的余音”中，一直是个非常滑稽的人物。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say that against this backdrop, it's hard to see him in quite the same entertaining light as previously.
sentences.zh: 我认为公平地说，在这种背景下，很难再像以前那样以同样娱乐的眼光看待他了。

sentences.en: So the Hindenburg circle decide, okay, let's talk to the Nazis after all.
sentences.zh: 所以兴登堡圈子决定，好吧，还是和纳粹谈谈吧。

sentences.en: And they do it through the press baron, Alfred Hugenberg, nationalist press baron, who I talked about in the previous podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们通过报业大亨阿尔弗雷德·胡根贝格进行接触，就是我在上一期播客中提到的那位民族主义报业大亨。

sentences.en: Von Papen is this great intriguer.
sentences.zh: 冯·帕彭是个伟大的阴谋家。

sentences.en: He is the key figure.
sentences.zh: 他是关键人物。

sentences.en: They have talks with Hitler and they say, maybe we'll put you in as chancellor after all.
sentences.zh: 他们与希特勒进行了会谈，并说，也许我们最终还是会让你担任总理。

sentences.en: But most of your cabinet have to be conservatives, not Nazis.
sentences.zh: 但你的内阁成员大部分必须是保守派，而不是纳粹。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, they hear talks that Schleicher may be, General Schleicher may be planning some sort of coup.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们听到传闻说施莱谢尔，施莱谢尔将军可能在策划某种政变。

sentences.en: So they're very exercised by this.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对此非常焦虑。

sentences.en: They say, we must hurry, we must hurry, we must sort this out so that Schleicher doesn't get in instead.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们必须抓紧，我们必须抓紧，我们必须解决这个问题，以免施莱谢尔抢先一步。

sentences.en: I mean, it's pure court politics.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这纯粹是宫廷政治。

sentences.en: The ideological divisions between Hindenburg, Papen, Schleicher are minimal.
sentences.zh: 兴登堡、帕彭、施莱谢尔之间的意识形态分歧微乎其微。

sentences.en: It's all Game of Thrones.
sentences.zh: 这完全就是《权力的游戏》。

sentences.en: It's very Game of Thrones.
sentences.zh: 非常有《权力的游戏》的感觉。

sentences.en: And Ian Kershaw says in his biography, you know, even at this point, if they had basically stopped intriguing against each other,
sentences.zh: 伊恩·克肖在他的传记中写道，你知道，即使在这一点上，如果他们基本上停止互相算计，

sentences.en: if Hindenburg had just said, listen, this is a shambles, let's dissolve the Reichstag, go on Schleicher, have a go, run the country, rearm, do what you like,
sentences.zh: 如果兴登堡只是说，听着，这简直是一团糟，让我们解散国会，去吧施莱谢尔，试一试，管理国家，重整军备，随你怎么做，

sentences.en: be a bit authoritarian, the Nazi regime could have been averted.
sentences.zh: 表现得稍微独裁一点，纳粹政权本是可以避免的。

sentences.en: But again, they don't know.
sentences.zh: 但他们还是不知道。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Schleicher thinks.
sentences.zh: 施莱谢尔认为。

sentences.en: That is a worse alternative.
sentences.zh: 那是更糟糕的选择。

sentences.en: No, they don't.
sentences.zh: 不，他们不知道。

sentences.en: Because Schleicher thinks, you know what, the Nazis maybe aren't so bad.
sentences.zh: 因为施莱谢尔认为，你知道吗，纳粹也许没那么坏。

sentences.en: I'll probably end up running the army.
sentences.zh: 我可能最终会掌管军队。

sentences.en: The Italy army will run things anyway.
sentences.zh: 反正军队会处理一切事务。

sentences.en: So, you know, who cares?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: And von Papen, he is convinced that he's been chancellor already.
sentences.zh: 而冯·帕彭，他确信自己已经当过总理了。

sentences.en: He thinks, you know, Hitler, this two-bit Austrian, it's fine, I'll run, I'll be his vice chancellor and I'll run things and the cabinet will be full of my friends.
sentences.zh: 他想，你知道，希特勒，这个三流奥地利人，没关系，我会管理，我会担任他的副总理，我会掌控局面，内阁里会坐满我的朋友。

sentences.en: So it is that on the 22nd of January, 1933, there is a crucial secret meeting between Hitler and Papen and Hindenburg's son, Oscar.
sentences.zh: 于是，在1933年1月22日，希特勒、帕彭和兴登堡的儿子奥斯卡之间进行了一次关键的秘密会晤。

sentences.en: It's at that meeting they do the deal and they agree that Hitler will be the chancellor and Papen will be his deputy.
sentences.zh: 就是在这次会议上，他们达成了交易，同意由希特勒担任总理，帕彭担任他的副手。

sentences.en: And Dominic, do you know what else happens on the 22nd of January, 1933?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你知道1933年1月22日还发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Is it some test match?
sentences.zh: 是什么板球测试赛吗？

sentences.en: No, Hitler goes to the grave of Horst Wessel because Hitler had not gone to Horst Wessel's funeral, but he goes to his grave and he addresses a memorial service in the evening.
sentences.zh: 不，希特勒去了霍斯特·威塞尔的墓前，因为希特勒没有参加霍斯特·威塞尔的葬礼，但他去了他的墓前，并在晚上发表了纪念演说。

sentences.en: And they play the funeral march from Gotterdammerung, from Wagner.
sentences.zh: 他们播放了瓦格纳《诸神的黄昏》中的葬礼进行曲。

sentences.en: And the stage is all set with laurel trees, with candelabras and with a huge, larger-than-life-size portrait of Wessel.
sentences.zh: 舞台上布置了月桂树、烛台，还有一幅巨大的、真人大小的威塞尔肖像。

sentences.en: So even as he is doing his kind of, you know, behind-the-scenes shenanigans and all that kind of stuff, he is also out on the public stage promoting this Nazi martyr.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使在他进行那种幕后勾当和所有那些事情的时候，他也在公共舞台上宣传这位纳粹烈士。

sentences.en: Well, doesn't that capture something about the Nazi rise to power?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这难道没有捕捉到纳粹夺取政权的一些本质吗？

sentences.en: That it's the combination of the backstairs, backroom, intriguing, and then these sort of lurid, pseudo-religious, theatrical spectacles.
sentences.zh: 那就是幕后交易、阴谋诡计，再加上那种耸人听闻的、伪宗教的、戏剧性的奇观的结合。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so with that, so from that moment, the deal is done.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，从那一刻起，交易达成了。

sentences.en: And on the 30th of January, Hitler goes into Hindenburg's apartment at the Reich's Chancellery, Wilhelm Straß, if you remember from the first episode.
sentences.zh: 1月30日，希特勒进入了位于威廉大街的帝国总理府兴登堡的公寓，如果你还记得第一集的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, the palace was being renovated.
sentences.zh: 是的，那座宫殿当时正在翻修。

sentences.en: And they do the deal, and Hindenburg says, and now, gentlemen, forwards with God.
sentences.zh: 他们达成了交易，兴登堡说，现在，先生们，以上帝之名，前进吧。

sentences.en: And somebody says to von Papen about that time, how can you work with these vulgar, stupid, utterly inexperienced, extremely violent, sort of common men?
